newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury sees $50 bln Q1 borrowing need.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury sees $50 bln Q1 borrowing need.

text.p: The Treasury Department announced on Monday that its net market borrowing need during the first quarter this year will be about $50 billion.
That will leave Treasury with a cash balance of $20 billion on March 31.
During the October-December fourth quarter last year, Treasury's actual net market borrowing was $41.3 billion and it ended the quarter with a $32.8-billion cash balance.
That was less than the $48-billion Treasury had estimated last October that it would borrow in the fourth quarter, when it foresaw an end-of-year balance of $30 billion.
"The combined $9.5-billion improvement was the result of higher than estimated receipts and lower than estimated outlays," Treasury said.

Looking ahead to the second quarter this year, Treasury estimated it will pay down between $10 billion and $15 billion in the April-June period and that it will have a cash balance of $35 billion on June 30.

The second quarter typically results in a paydown of debts because it includes the April 15 filing deadline for individual income tax returns so the government receives more revenues and has less need to borrow.
Treasury will announce on Wednesday its plans for selling three- and 10-year notes as well as 30-year bonds next week to meet its borrowing needs for the current first quarter.
